newsitem.title: USA: IBM surges after split, pushing Dow higher.
newsitem.headline: IBM surges after split, pushing Dow higher.

text.p: International Business Machines Corp shares jumped nearly five percent in heavy trading on Friday.
The world's largest computer maker announced it would split its stock, doubling the number of shares available for trading.
The shares were up 7-1/8 to 152-1/2 in heavy late morning trading, accounting for about 20 points of the Dow industrials' 75-point surge.
Salomon Brothers analyst John Jones upgraded the stock to strong buy from buy but did not comment further.

Although the stock had been climbing steadily since January, IBM shares have been battered in the last few sessions, losing about 22 points after IBM posted fourth quarter profits last week that disappointed Wall Street.
It said last Tuesday that earnings rose 18 percent to $2 billion or $3.93 a share in the quarter, but some analysts said they were disappointed by sluggish mainframe sales.
IBM also today set an unchanged quarterly dividend of $0.35 a share presplit.

Daniel Ries, analyst for Nomura Securities, said of the stock split, "It's mainly a psychological move. I suppose it makes the stock more affordable to smaller retail accounts who don't want to shell out $15,000 for 100 shares of IBM stock, but in terms of institutional investors it has no impact and it does not impact the income model."

Although the slide in IBM's stock price has been halted for now, "I wouldn't look for a meaningful move in the stock until they in some way reassure investors that hardware (revenues) will grow in the eight percent range," Ries said.
Disappointing growth in hardware sales and continued economic problems in European markets caused analysts to slash ratings on IBM, one of the 1996 market's most powerful share price locomotives.

Analysts point to concerns about the impact of a stronger dollar and European economic sluggishness, along with IBM-specific growth issues, especially in hardware sales, which increased only two percent during the final quarter of 1996.
